I’m at Tolo Harbour, heading to Ikea. The almanac says today is a good day to move house, so Mom told me to go to Ikea and find my aunt. She was eating lobster there. I ran up to the third floor looking for her, then patted my trouser pocket and found only a pile of coins—no money for a taxi. I hoped Aunt wouldn’t blame me for being late. Searching for my aunt, I looked like an idiot. Finally, I found someone in a corner who looked like “beautiful as a flower.” Sure enough, this “beautiful as a flower” was my aunt. No one was sitting beside her. As soon as she saw me, she joked, “You scumbag—making a pretty girl wait this long. Are you even human?” I said, “You were sitting here eating lobster. I was stuck in traffic from Tolo Harbour to Ikea all this time.” Aunt said, “Whatever. Let’s walk around Ikea and see what suits me for moving house.” I dragged this “beautiful as a flower” around, and everyone else thought I looked cool. Aunt paid the bill, so I saved another pile of coins. Eventually we got tired and went home separately. After getting home, I boldly asked Dad why Aunt looked so much like “beautiful as a flower.” Dad slapped me, and I got dizzy.
